# Design: Concurrent-claim race detection (issue #2534)

## Decision

GitHub's label API has no check-and-set: two runs can both read "no claim" and both add
`zbuild:claimed`, each getting a success reply. After adding the label (gh backend only),
the coordinator posts a concurrent claim note — `"concurrent claim by \`<holder>\`"` —
then re-reads the GitHub issue itself (its labels or state), then reads back all trusted
concurrent claim notes. The note is the synchronous holder record (RQTIE-3 path 1). The
run whose note is first by GitHub's `created_at` (then `id` on a tie) is the winner; it
returns `{"acquired": true}`. Every other run marks its note "not started — concurrent
claim: `<winner>` was first" and returns
`{"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner>", "race_lost": true}`. The engine receives
`race_lost: true` and refuses immediately, skipping the stale-takeover path that would
otherwise trigger for any cross-machine refusal. ADR-005 gains §5 to document all of this.

Why the stale-takeover path cannot set `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED` for a race-lost response:
in `zbuild_claim_acquire`, the new `race_lost: true` branch (DSRACE-5) returns 1 before
the code reaches `_zbuild_claim_takeover`, so the takeover's `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED="$issue"`
assignment is never reached. DSRACE-4 is [code] because that guarantee requires DSRACE-5 to
be in place; without it, the existing takeover path can and does set `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED`.

Reviewed alternatives: GitHub's `labeled` events are not usable as the tie-break — GitHub
does not create a second `labeled` event when the label is already there, so the events
give no information about concurrent adders. The local-fs test backend is unaffected; its
`flock`-serialised add already returns rc 2 for a duplicate add.

Outside assumptions:
- `rsc_gh` and `jq` are available in the coordinator (already used throughout `plugin.sh`)
- GitHub's comment `created_at` and `id` are ordered and stable (standard API guarantee)
- The concurrent claim note format (`"concurrent claim by \`"`) is distinct from takeover
  notes (`"took over a stale claim from \`"`) — no interference

```steps
- 1 Add `_ccgl_self_holder_v`, `_ccgl_race_note_post_v`, `_ccgl_race_note_delete`, `_ccgl_race_note_update`, `_ccgl_race_note_first_v` to plugin.sh; extend `claim_coordinator_claim` to: post the concurrent claim note, re-read the GitHub issue, then read back concurrent claim notes, returning `race_lost: true` for the loser (gh backend only) | areas: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | serves: DSRACE-1, DSRACE-2, DSRACE-3, DSRACE-7
- 2 In `zbuild_claim_acquire`, detect `race_lost: true` in the refused reply and refuse immediately (skip stale-takeover, print concurrent-winner message) | areas: core/claim/claim.sh | serves: DSRACE-4, DSRACE-5
- 3 Amend ADR-005: add §5 (concurrent claim detection: arbitration note, first-by-created_at-then-id wins, loser updates note to not-started, `race_lost` skip); extend `Enforced by` | areas: docs/adr/ADR-005-claim-coordinator.md | serves: DSRACE-6
```

```acceptance
DSRACE-1[code]: After successfully adding the zbuild:claimed label (gh backend), the claim posts a concurrent claim note with the run's holder, then reads back all trusted concurrent claim notes to detect concurrent claimants covers: RQTIE-1, RQTIE-3
  Given: the zbuild:claimed label was just successfully added via the gh backend
  When: the claim posts a "concurrent claim by `<holder>`" note and reads back all trusted concurrent claim notes since the note's own created_at minus the detection window
  Then: the note is posted synchronously before the read-back
  And: all concurrent claim notes from the current label epoch are returned

DSRACE-2[code]: Only the run whose concurrent claim note is first (by created_at, then id) returns {"acquired": true}; all others return {"acquired": false} covers: RQTIE-2, RQTIE-1
  Given: two or more concurrent claim notes exist for the same issue within the detection window
  When: each run compares the notes and identifies the first
  Then: the run whose note has the earliest created_at returns {"acquired": true}
  And: all other runs return {"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner_holder>", "race_lost": true}

DSRACE-3[code]: The losing run updates its concurrent claim note body to "not started" covers: RQCMT-1
  Given: the run's concurrent claim note is not the first by created_at (or id)
  When: the run determines it has lost the race
  Then: the run PATCHes its note body to "not started — concurrent claim: `<winner>` was first"

DSRACE-4[code]: When zbuild_claim_acquire receives {"acquired": false, "race_lost": true} from the coordinator, _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is not set and zbuild_claim_release does not remove the zbuild:claimed label covers: RQLBL-1
  Given: claim_coordinator_claim returns {"acquired": false, "race_lost": true}
  When: zbuild_claim_acquire processes the response
  Then: _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED is not set
  And: zbuild_claim_release does not remove the zbuild:claimed label

DSRACE-5[code]: A coordinator response with race_lost: true causes zbuild_claim_acquire to refuse immediately without entering the stale-takeover path, printing a message that names the concurrent winner covers: RQTIE-1
  Given: claim_coordinator_claim returns {"acquired": false, "holder": "<winner>", "race_lost": true}
  When: zbuild_claim_acquire processes the response
  Then: the stale-takeover hook is not called
  And: stderr names the concurrent winner as the first claimant

DSRACE-6[doc]: ADR-005 §5 tells a reader: after adding the label (gh backend), a note is posted as the holder record, the first note by created_at then id wins, the loser marks its note "not started", and race_lost: true in the refused response skips the stale-takeover path covers: RQADR-1

DSRACE-7[code]: After posting the concurrent claim note (the synchronous holder record, gh backend), the claim reads back the GitHub issue's current state before proceeding with arbitration covers: RQREB-1
  Given: the zbuild:claimed label was added and the concurrent claim note was posted synchronously
  When: the claim reads the GitHub issue's current labels or state
  Then: fresh issue data is obtained from GitHub after the synchronous holder record was written

WIRING: core/claim/claim.sh
```

# Every gh call runs under the run-status comment's watchdog (rsc_gh,
# ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_GH_TIMEOUT): a hung gh in the exit path could otherwise
# only be KILLed, and would leave the label behind.
_ccgl_gh_lib() {
    declare -F rsc_gh >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    # shellcheck source=../../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
    source "${_ZBUILD_ROOT:-$_CCGL_DIR/../../..}/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
}
_CCGL_OUT=""
_ccgl_gh() {
    _ccgl_gh_lib || return 1
    local out rc=0
    out="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ccgl-gh.XXXXXX")" || return 1
    rsc_gh "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}" "$out" "$@" || rc=$?
    _CCGL_OUT="$(cat "$out" 2>/dev/null)"
    rm -f "$out"
    return "$rc"
}

# The repository every label call and the holder reader name: one slug, the
# same for both (GITHUB_REPOSITORY in CI, else the origin's). rc 1 when none.
_CCGL_SLUG=""
_ccgl_slug() {
    [[ -n "$_CCGL_SLUG" ]] && return 0
    _ccgl_gh_lib || return 1
    _CCGL_SLUG="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
    [[ -n "$_CCGL_SLUG" ]] || _CCGL_SLUG="$(zbuild_repo_slug 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_CCGL_SLUG" ]]
}

# Labels on an issue, one a line, into _CCGL_OUT. rc 1 on a backend error.
_ccgl_read_labels() {
    local issue="$1"
    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
        gh) _ccgl_slug && _ccgl_gh issue view "$issue" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" ;;
        local-fs)
            local f; f="$(_ccgl_lf_labels_file "$issue")"
            _CCGL_OUT=""
            [[ -f "$f" ]] && _CCGL_OUT="$(cat "$f")"
            return 0 ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

# rc 0 when <label> is on <issue> now (one read).
_ccgl_label_on() {
    local line
    _ccgl_read_labels "$1" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r line; do [[ "$line" == "$2" ]] && return 0; done <<< "$_CCGL_OUT"
    return 1
}

# Add the label. rc 0 added, 2 already there (local-fs: checked inside the lock),
# 1 backend error. A repository that does not define the label yet gets it once.
_ccgl_add_label() {
    local issue="$1" label="$2"
    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
        gh)
            _ccgl_slug || return 1
            _ccgl_gh issue edit "$issue" --add-label "$label" --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" && return 0
            if [[ "$_RSC_GH_ERR" == *"not found"* ]]; then
                _ccgl_gh label create "$label" --force --color "5319e7" \
                    --description "a zbuild run is working on this issue" --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" || return 1
                _ccgl_gh issue edit "$issue" --add-label "$label" --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" && return 0
            fi
            # The add may have reached GitHub with its answer lost (a timeout, a
            # dropped reply). The issue was clear when read, so a label there now
            # is this run's: say so, or nothing would ever release it.
            _ccgl_label_on "$issue" "$label"
            ;;
        local-fs)
            local f; f="$(_ccgl_lf_labels_file "$issue")"
            local timeout; timeout="$(_ccgl_flock_timeout_sec)"
            (
                exec 9>"${f}.lock"
                flock -w "$timeout" 9 || exit 1
                touch "$f"
                grep -Fxq "$label" "$f" && exit 2
                echo "$label" >> "$f"
                exit 0
            )
            ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

_ccgl_remove_label() {
    local issue="$1" label="$2"
    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
        gh) _ccgl_slug && _ccgl_gh issue edit "$issue" --remove-label "$label" --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG" ;;
        local-fs)
            local f; f="$(_ccgl_lf_labels_file "$issue")"
            [[ ! -f "$f" ]] && return 0
            local timeout; timeout="$(_ccgl_flock_timeout_sec)"
            (
                exec 9>"${f}.lock"
                flock -w "$timeout" 9 || exit 1
                grep -Fxv "$label" "$f" > "${f}.new" || true
                mv "${f}.new" "$f"
            )
            ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
}

# _ccgl_read_holder <issue> — who the newest run-status comment names as holder.
_ccgl_read_holder() {
    local issue="$1" holder=""
    _ccgl_gh_lib || return 0
    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
        local-fs)
            local rsc="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE:-}/$issue/run-status-comment.txt"
            [[ -f "$rsc" ]] || return 0
            rsc_holder_line_v holder "$(cat "$rsc")"
            printf '%s' "$holder"
            ;;
        gh)
            _ccgl_slug || return 0
            rsc_holder_find "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}" "$_CCGL_SLUG" "$issue"
            ;;
    esac
}

_ccgl_refused() {
    local issue="$1" holder
    holder="$(_ccgl_read_holder "$issue" || true)"
    jq -nc --arg h "$holder" '{acquired: false, holder: $h}'
    printf 'claim-coordinator: issue #%s carries the %s label: another run is working on it. If that run is gone, remove the label: gh issue edit %s --remove-label %s\n' \
        "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" >&2 || true
}

# ─── Hook: claim <issue_id> ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# stdout: {"acquired": true} | {"acquired": false, "holder": "<holder>"}
#         | {"acquired": false, "skipped": "<why>"} (no claim was attempted)
# rc: 0 answered, 1 backend error, 2 usage error.
claim_coordinator_claim() {
    local issue="$1"
    [[ -z "$issue" ]] && { printf 'claim_coordinator_claim: missing issue id\n' >&2 || true; return 2; }
    # The label is on GitHub (local-fs stands in for it): a run told to stay off
    # GitHub makes no claim there.
    if [[ "${NO_GITHUB:-}" == "true" ]]; then
        printf '{"acquired": false, "skipped": "NO_GITHUB=true"}\n'
        return 0
    fi

    if ! _ccgl_read_labels "$issue"; then
        printf '{"acquired": false, "reason": "backend_read_error"}\n'
        return 1
    fi
    local line
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ "$line" == "$_CCGL_LABEL" ]] && { _ccgl_refused "$issue"; return 0; }
    done <<< "$_CCGL_OUT"

    # No hostname in the label: a laptop run and a CI run claim the same one.
    local add_rc=0
    _ccgl_add_label "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" || add_rc=$?
    if [[ "$add_rc" -eq 2 ]]; then
        _ccgl_refused "$issue"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "$add_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
        printf '{"acquired": false, "reason": "backend_error"}\n'
        return 1
    fi
    printf '{"acquired": true}\n'
    return 0
}

# ─── Hook: release <issue_id> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
claim_coordinator_release() {
    local issue="$1"
    [[ -z "$issue" ]] && { printf 'claim_coordinator_release: missing issue id\n' >&2 || true; return 2; }
    _ccgl_remove_label "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" && return 0
    printf 'claim-coordinator: could not remove %s from issue #%s — remove the %s label by hand, or the next run of the issue is refused.\n' \
        "$_CCGL_LABEL" "$issue" "$_CCGL_LABEL" >&2 || true
    return 1
}

# ─── Hook: heartbeat <issue_id> ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Labels do not expire (a stale claim is #2533's).
claim_coordinator_heartbeat() {
    return 0
}

# ─── Hook: takeover <issue> <holder> <by> <stale_s> <state_dir> ───────────────
# ADR-005 §3 (#2616): a claim another machine holds, judged on GitHub's clock
# and taken over when stale (lib/takeover.sh, loaded only here): released, and
# claimed again for this run. stdout: {"taken_over":true,"claimed":true,"age_s":N}
# | {"taken_over":false[,"failed":"<why>"]}.
claim_coordinator_takeover() {
    if ! declare -F claim_takeover_run >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        local _lrc=0
        # shellcheck source=lib/takeover.sh
        source "$_CCGL_DIR/lib/takeover.sh" 2>/dev/null || _lrc=$?
        if (( _lrc != 0 )) || ! declare -F claim_takeover_run >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: takeover.sh could not be loaded (%s) — refusing to take over %s\n' "$_CCGL_DIR/lib/takeover.sh" "${2:-}" >&2
            printf '{"taken_over":false}\n'; return 0
        fi
    fi
    claim_takeover_run "$1" "$2" "$3" "$4" "$5" claim_coordinator_release claim_coordinator_claim
}

# ─── Hook: list_claims ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# stdout: JSON array of {issue, holder, acquired_at}. rc 1 on a backend error.
claim_coordinator_list_claims() {
    case "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_BACKEND:-gh}" in
        gh)
            { _ccgl_slug && _ccgl_gh issue list --label "$_CCGL_LABEL" --json number --repo "$_CCGL_SLUG"; } || {
                printf 'list_claims: gh issue list failed\n' >&2 || true
                return 1
            }
            jq -c 'map({issue: .number, holder: "unknown", acquired_at: null})' <<< "$_CCGL_OUT" 2>/dev/null \
                || printf '[]\n'
            ;;
        local-fs)
            local store="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_STORE:?}"
            local results='[]' issue_dir issue holder
            for issue_dir in "$store"/*/; do
                [[ -f "$issue_dir/labels.txt" ]] || continue
                grep -Fxq "$_CCGL_LABEL" "$issue_dir/labels.txt" 2>/dev/null || continue
                issue="${issue_dir%/}"; issue="${issue##*/}"
                holder="$(_ccgl_read_holder "$issue" || true)"
                results="$(jq -c --arg i "$issue" --arg h "$holder" \
                    '. + [{issue: ($i|tonumber), holder: $h, acquired_at: null}]' <<< "$results")"
            done
            printf '%s\n' "$results"
            ;;
        *) printf '[]\n' ;;
    esac
    return 0
}

4	# the first stage and to release it on exit, through the plugin registry. What
5	# a claim is (a label, a lease) is the coordinator's business, not this file's.
6	# Sourced by runner.sh; uses the registry and the event bus it has loaded.

9	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_SH_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0

12	_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED=""        # the issue this run holds the claim on
13	_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR=""       # the coordinator that gave it
14	_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER=""    # who holds the claim that refused this run

16	# ADR-005 §3 (#2533): heartbeat and staleness thresholds.
17	: "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_S:=600}"   # seconds between heartbeat flushes

20	# The coordinator: the first claim-coordinator plugin under the plugins root,

22	_zbuild_claim_coordinator_v() {
23	    local -n _zcc_out="$1"

32	    return 0
33	}

35	# Who this run is, as it names itself to a run that finds its claim: the CI
36	# run's URL, or the run id and the machine (ZBUILD_CLAIM_MACHINE_ID overrides).
37	_zbuild_claim_holder_v() {
38	    local -n _zch_out="$1"
39	    if [[ "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" == "true" ]]; then
40	        _zch_out="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-unknown}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-unknown}"
41	    else
42	        # #2589: the runner's pid, so a later run on this machine can tell a

44	        _zch_out="run_id=${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-} machine=${ZBUILD_CLAIM_MACHINE_ID:-${HOSTNAME:-unknown}} pid=$$"

48	# A claim the engine could not make: the run goes on (ADR-005 §3), visibly.
49	_zbuild_claim_skipped() {

51	    printf 'zbuild: no cross-machine claim on issue #%s (%s) — the run goes on unclaimed\n' "$1" "$2" >&2 || true

53	
54	# zbuild_claim_acquire <issue> <state_dir> — rc 0: claimed, or no claim made
55	# (no issue, no coordinator, the coordinator failed or skipped); rc 1: refused —
56	# another run holds it (its holder in _ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER), or the
57	# coordinator's answer cannot be read, which may hide a claim that is there.
58	zbuild_claim_acquire() {

60	    _ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER=""
61	    [[ "$issue" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || return 0

67	    fi

70	    local reply_file="$state_dir/runtime/claim-reply.json" reply="" rc=0
71	    [[ -d "${reply_file%/*}" ]] || mkdir -p "${reply_file%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true
72	    plugin_hook_call "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" claim "$issue" > "$reply_file" || rc=$?
73	    IFS= read -r -d '' reply < "$reply_file" || true
74	    # A JSON string cannot hold an unescaped quote, so a holder's text never
75	    # matches these. A reply that says acquired is believed whatever the hook's
76	    # status (#2586): an interrupt can cut the wait short after the label went
77	    # on, and a claim this run made must be released by it. A trapped signal
78	    # that lands while bash waits on the hook makes `wait` return 128+signal at
79	    # once; on a busy runner that is often (#2591: 27 of 60 under load, Ubuntu

85	    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"acquired\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]; then

97	    fi
98	    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"acquired\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*false ]]; then
99	        _ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER="$(jq -r '.holder // empty' <<< "$reply" 2>/dev/null || true)"

102	        # crashed, or was killed, before releasing) is cleared, once, and the
103	        # claim taken again. Another machine's, or CI's, is never touched.
104	        local _zca_own=""; _zbuild_claim_own_v _zca_own "$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER"
105	        # A resumed run finds its own claim (same run id, this machine): it is
106	        # this run's again (review of #2589).
107	        if [[ "$_zca_own" == mine ]]; then
108	            _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED="$issue"
109	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.acquired" "issue=$issue" "holder=$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" 2>/dev/null || true
110	            return 0
111	        fi
112	        if [[ -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_RETRIED:-}" && "$_zca_own" == stale ]]; then
113	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.stale_cleared" "issue=$issue" "holder=$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" 2>/dev/null || true
114	            printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: clearing a claim this machine left (%s) on issue %s\n' "$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" "$issue" >&2

116	            local _zca_rc=0
117	            _ZBUILD_CLAIM_RETRIED=1 zbuild_claim_acquire "$issue" "$state_dir" || _zca_rc=$?
118	            return "$_zca_rc"
119	        elif [[ -z "$_zca_own" && -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_RETRIED:-}" ]]; then

127	    if [[ -n "$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" ]]; then

134	# _zbuild_claim_own_v <var> <holder> — what a local holder on this machine is to

138	_zbuild_claim_own_v() {

140	    _zco=""

144	    kill -0 "${BASH_REMATCH[3]}" 2>/dev/null || _zco=stale

146	}

149	# and on a second call. Never fails the caller: a failure is an event.
150	zbuild_claim_release() {
151	    local issue="${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}"
152	    [[ -n "$issue" ]] || return 0
153	    _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED=""
154	    local rc=0
155	    plugin_hook_call "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" release "$issue" >/dev/null || rc=$?
156	    if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
157	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.release_failed" "issue=$issue" "rc=$rc" 2>/dev/null || true
158	    fi
159	    return 0
160	}
161	
162	# _zbuild_claim_stale_s_v <var> — ZBUILD_CLAIM_STALE_S as a number; one that is
163	# not (e.g. "30m") is the default, 1800, not 0 (#2533 review: 0 made every
164	# claim stale).
165	# One shorter than two heartbeats would make a live run stale between two of
166	# them: it is raised to that.
167	_zbuild_claim_stale_s_v() {
168	    local -n _zcs="$1"; local hb="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_S:-600}"
169	    _zcs="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_STALE_S:-1800}"
170	    [[ "$_zcs" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || _zcs=1800
171	    [[ "$hb" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || hb=600
172	    (( _zcs >= 2 * hb )) || _zcs=$(( 2 * hb ))
173	}
174	
175	# _zbuild_claim_takeover <issue> <state_dir> — ADR-005 §3 (#2533, #2616):
176	# another machine's (or CI's) claim, refused. Whether it is stale, and taking it
177	# over, is the coordinator's (its takeover hook); a coordinator with none refuses.
178	# rc as zbuild_claim_acquire.
179	_zbuild_claim_takeover() {
180	    local issue="$1" state_dir="$2" them="$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" stale me reply="" rc=0 _tk=""
181	    yaml_get_v _tk "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR/manifest.yaml" hooks.takeover 2>/dev/null || _tk=""
182	    if [[ -z "$_tk" ]]; then
183	        printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: the claim coordinator cannot judge a stale claim (no takeover hook) — refusing to take over %s\n' "$them" >&2
184	        return 1
185	    fi
186	    _zbuild_claim_stale_s_v stale
187	    _zbuild_claim_holder_v me
188	    local reply_file="$state_dir/runtime/claim-takeover-reply.json"
189	    [[ -d "${reply_file%/*}" ]] || mkdir -p "${reply_file%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true
190	    plugin_hook_call "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" takeover "$issue" "$them" "$me" "$stale" "$state_dir" > "$reply_file" || rc=$?
191	    IFS= read -r -d '' reply < "$reply_file" || true
192	    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"taken_over\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]; then
193	        local age=""; [[ "$reply" =~ \"age_s\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+) ]] && age="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
194	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.taken_over" "issue=$issue" "holder=$them" "age_s=$age" 2>/dev/null || true
195	        # The coordinator claimed it again for this run (review of #2616).
196	        if [[ "$reply" =~ \"claimed\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]; then
197	            _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED="$issue"
198	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.acquired" "issue=$issue" "holder=$me" 2>/dev/null || true
199	            return 0
200	        fi
201	        local arc=0
202	        _ZBUILD_CLAIM_RETRIED=1 zbuild_claim_acquire "$issue" "$state_dir" || arc=$?
203	        return "$arc"
204	    fi
205	    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"failed\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"([a-z_]+)\" ]]; then
206	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.takeover_failed" "issue=$issue" "holder=$them" "reason=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" 2>/dev/null || true
207	    elif [[ "$rc" -ne 0 || ! "$reply" =~ \"taken_over\" ]]; then
208	        printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: the claim coordinator'"'"'s takeover gave no answer (rc=%s) — refusing to take over %s\n' "$rc" "$them" >&2
209	    fi
210	    return 1
211	}
212	
213	# zbuild_claim_heartbeat_say <status-comment-pid> — R5 (#2533): a run that
214	# posts no run-status comment says its claim has no heartbeat, so another
215	# machine ages it from when its label was added. Nothing when it has one, or
216	# holds no claim.
217	zbuild_claim_heartbeat_say() {
218	    [[ -n "${1:-}" || -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}" ]] && return 0
219	    printf 'zbuild: this run posts no run-status comment, so its claim has no heartbeat — another machine ages it from when its label was added\n' >&2
220	}

# core/claim/claim.sh — the engine's side of the cross-machine claim (ADR-005).
# The engine asks the claim coordinator plugin to claim the run's issue before
# the first stage and to release it on exit, through the plugin registry. What
# a claim is (a label, a lease) is the coordinator's business, not this file's.
# Sourced by runner.sh; uses the registry and the event bus it has loaded.
# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_SH_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_CLAIM_SH_LOADED=1

_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED=""        # the issue this run holds the claim on
_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR=""       # the coordinator that gave it
_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER=""    # who holds the claim that refused this run

# ADR-005 §3 (#2533): heartbeat and staleness thresholds.
: "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_S:=600}"   # seconds between heartbeat flushes
: "${ZBUILD_CLAIM_STALE_S:=1800}"      # seconds before a cross-machine claim is stale

# The coordinator: the first claim-coordinator plugin under the plugins root,
# found as every other plugin is.
_zbuild_claim_coordinator_v() {
    local -n _zcc_out="$1"
    _zcc_out=""
    local -a _zcc_dirs=()
    local _zcc_d _zcc_kind
    discover_plugins_into _zcc_dirs "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    for _zcc_d in ${_zcc_dirs[@]+"${_zcc_dirs[@]}"}; do
        yaml_get_v _zcc_kind "$_zcc_d/manifest.yaml" kind 2>/dev/null || continue
        [[ "$_zcc_kind" == "claim-coordinator" ]] && { _zcc_out="$_zcc_d"; return 0; }
    done
    return 0
}

# Who this run is, as it names itself to a run that finds its claim: the CI
# run's URL, or the run id and the machine (ZBUILD_CLAIM_MACHINE_ID overrides).
_zbuild_claim_holder_v() {
    local -n _zch_out="$1"
    if [[ "${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}" == "true" ]]; then
        _zch_out="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-unknown}/actions/runs/${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-unknown}"
    else
        # #2589: the runner's pid, so a later run on this machine can tell a
        # live holder from one that crashed (kill -0), with no slot needed.
        _zch_out="run_id=${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-} machine=${ZBUILD_CLAIM_MACHINE_ID:-${HOSTNAME:-unknown}} pid=$$"
    fi
}

# A claim the engine could not make: the run goes on (ADR-005 §3), visibly.
_zbuild_claim_skipped() {
    eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.skipped" "issue=$1" "reason=$2" 2>/dev/null || true
    printf 'zbuild: no cross-machine claim on issue #%s (%s) — the run goes on unclaimed\n' "$1" "$2" >&2 || true
}

# zbuild_claim_acquire <issue> <state_dir> — rc 0: claimed, or no claim made
# (no issue, no coordinator, the coordinator failed or skipped); rc 1: refused —
# another run holds it (its holder in _ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER), or the
# coordinator's answer cannot be read, which may hide a claim that is there.
zbuild_claim_acquire() {
    local issue="$1" state_dir="$2"
    _ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER=""
    [[ "$issue" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || return 0

    _zbuild_claim_coordinator_v _ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR
    if [[ -z "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" ]]; then
        _zbuild_claim_skipped "$issue" "no claim-coordinator plugin installed"
        return 0
    fi

    # The reply goes through a file: a $( ) would copy the whole engine shell.
    local reply_file="$state_dir/runtime/claim-reply.json" reply="" rc=0
    [[ -d "${reply_file%/*}" ]] || mkdir -p "${reply_file%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true
    plugin_hook_call "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" claim "$issue" > "$reply_file" || rc=$?
    IFS= read -r -d '' reply < "$reply_file" || true
    # A JSON string cannot hold an unescaped quote, so a holder's text never
    # matches these. A reply that says acquired is believed whatever the hook's
    # status (#2586): an interrupt can cut the wait short after the label went
    # on, and a claim this run made must be released by it. A trapped signal
    # that lands while bash waits on the hook makes `wait` return 128+signal at
    # once; on a busy runner that is often (#2591: 27 of 60 under load, Ubuntu
    # 26.04, every claim made and released).
    if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 && ! "$reply" =~ \"acquired\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]; then
        _zbuild_claim_skipped "$issue" "the claim coordinator failed (rc=$rc)"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"acquired\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]; then
        _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED="$issue"
        local holder; _zbuild_claim_holder_v holder
        eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.acquired" "issue=$issue" "holder=$holder" 2>/dev/null || true
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"skipped\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"([^\"\\]*)\" ]]; then
        _zbuild_claim_skipped "$issue" "${BASH_REMATCH[1]//[[:cntrl:]]/}"
        return 0
    elif [[ "$reply" =~ \"skipped\"[[:space:]]*: ]]; then
        _zbuild_claim_skipped "$issue" "the claim coordinator made no claim"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"acquired\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*false ]]; then
        _ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER="$(jq -r '.holder // empty' <<< "$reply" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        _ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER="${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER//[[:cntrl:]]/}"
        # #2589 (ADR-005): a claim this machine's own run left behind (it
        # crashed, or was killed, before releasing) is cleared, once, and the
        # claim taken again. Another machine's, or CI's, is never touched.
        local _zca_own=""; _zbuild_claim_own_v _zca_own "$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER"
        # A resumed run finds its own claim (same run id, this machine): it is
        # this run's again (review of #2589).
        if [[ "$_zca_own" == mine ]]; then
            _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED="$issue"
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.acquired" "issue=$issue" "holder=$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" 2>/dev/null || true
            return 0
        fi
        if [[ -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_RETRIED:-}" && "$_zca_own" == stale ]]; then
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.stale_cleared" "issue=$issue" "holder=$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" 2>/dev/null || true
            printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: clearing a claim this machine left (%s) on issue %s\n' "$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" "$issue" >&2
            plugin_hook_call "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" release "$issue" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            local _zca_rc=0
            _ZBUILD_CLAIM_RETRIED=1 zbuild_claim_acquire "$issue" "$state_dir" || _zca_rc=$?
            return "$_zca_rc"
        elif [[ -z "$_zca_own" && -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_RETRIED:-}" ]]; then
            # ADR-005 §3 (#2533, #2616): cross-machine stale takeover, the
            # coordinator's (its takeover hook).
            _zbuild_claim_takeover "$issue" "$state_dir"
            return $?
        fi
    fi
    # Refused — holder named in _ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER; print it for the caller.
    if [[ -n "$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" ]]; then
        printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: issue #%s is held by %s — refused\n' \
            "$issue" "$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" >&2
    fi
    return 1
}

# _zbuild_claim_own_v <var> <holder> — what a local holder on this machine is to
# this run: "mine" (this run's id: a resume), "stale" (another run here whose
# pid is gone), or "" (anything else: another machine, CI, a live run, or a
# holder written before pids were — never cleared).
_zbuild_claim_own_v() {
    local -n _zco="$1"; local h="$2" me="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_MACHINE_ID:-${HOSTNAME:-unknown}}"
    _zco=""
    [[ "$h" =~ ^run_id=([^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+machine=([^[:space:]]+)[[:space:]]+pid=([0-9]+)$ ]] || return 0
    [[ "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}" == "$me" ]] || return 0
    if [[ "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" == "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" ]]; then _zco=mine; return 0; fi
    kill -0 "${BASH_REMATCH[3]}" 2>/dev/null || _zco=stale
    return 0
}

# zbuild_claim_release — release the claim this run holds; a no-op otherwise,
# and on a second call. Never fails the caller: a failure is an event.
zbuild_claim_release() {
    local issue="${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}"
    [[ -n "$issue" ]] || return 0
    _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED=""
    local rc=0
    plugin_hook_call "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" release "$issue" >/dev/null || rc=$?
    if [[ "$rc" -ne 0 ]]; then
        eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.release_failed" "issue=$issue" "rc=$rc" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    return 0
}

# _zbuild_claim_stale_s_v <var> — ZBUILD_CLAIM_STALE_S as a number; one that is
# not (e.g. "30m") is the default, 1800, not 0 (#2533 review: 0 made every
# claim stale).
# One shorter than two heartbeats would make a live run stale between two of
# them: it is raised to that.
_zbuild_claim_stale_s_v() {
    local -n _zcs="$1"; local hb="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_HEARTBEAT_S:-600}"
    _zcs="${ZBUILD_CLAIM_STALE_S:-1800}"
    [[ "$_zcs" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || _zcs=1800
    [[ "$hb" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || hb=600
    (( _zcs >= 2 * hb )) || _zcs=$(( 2 * hb ))
}

# _zbuild_claim_takeover <issue> <state_dir> — ADR-005 §3 (#2533, #2616):
# another machine's (or CI's) claim, refused. Whether it is stale, and taking it
# over, is the coordinator's (its takeover hook); a coordinator with none refuses.
# rc as zbuild_claim_acquire.
_zbuild_claim_takeover() {
    local issue="$1" state_dir="$2" them="$_ZBUILD_CLAIM_THEIR_HOLDER" stale me reply="" rc=0 _tk=""
    yaml_get_v _tk "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR/manifest.yaml" hooks.takeover 2>/dev/null || _tk=""
    if [[ -z "$_tk" ]]; then
        printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: the claim coordinator cannot judge a stale claim (no takeover hook) — refusing to take over %s\n' "$them" >&2
        return 1
    fi
    _zbuild_claim_stale_s_v stale
    _zbuild_claim_holder_v me
    local reply_file="$state_dir/runtime/claim-takeover-reply.json"
    [[ -d "${reply_file%/*}" ]] || mkdir -p "${reply_file%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true
    plugin_hook_call "$_ZBUILD_COORDINATOR_DIR" takeover "$issue" "$them" "$me" "$stale" "$state_dir" > "$reply_file" || rc=$?
    IFS= read -r -d '' reply < "$reply_file" || true
    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"taken_over\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]; then
        local age=""; [[ "$reply" =~ \"age_s\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+) ]] && age="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.taken_over" "issue=$issue" "holder=$them" "age_s=$age" 2>/dev/null || true
        # The coordinator claimed it again for this run (review of #2616).
        if [[ "$reply" =~ \"claimed\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]; then
            _ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED="$issue"
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.acquired" "issue=$issue" "holder=$me" 2>/dev/null || true
            return 0
        fi
        local arc=0
        _ZBUILD_CLAIM_RETRIED=1 zbuild_claim_acquire "$issue" "$state_dir" || arc=$?
        return "$arc"
    fi
    if [[ "$reply" =~ \"failed\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"([a-z_]+)\" ]]; then
        eb_emit_event "pipeline.claim.takeover_failed" "issue=$issue" "holder=$them" "reason=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" 2>/dev/null || true
    elif [[ "$rc" -ne 0 || ! "$reply" =~ \"taken_over\" ]]; then
        printf 'zbuild_claim_acquire: the claim coordinator'"'"'s takeover gave no answer (rc=%s) — refusing to take over %s\n' "$rc" "$them" >&2
    fi
    return 1
}

# zbuild_claim_heartbeat_say <status-comment-pid> — R5 (#2533): a run that
# posts no run-status comment says its claim has no heartbeat, so another
# machine ages it from when its label was added. Nothing when it has one, or
# holds no claim.
zbuild_claim_heartbeat_say() {
    [[ -n "${1:-}" || -z "${_ZBUILD_CLAIM_ACQUIRED:-}" ]] && return 0
    printf 'zbuild: this run posts no run-status comment, so its claim has no heartbeat — another machine ages it from when its label was added\n' >&2
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/lib/claim-gh-mock.sh — a stateful mock `gh` for the github-labels claim
# coordinator (ADR-005). The issue's labels, whether the repository defines the
# label, and the comments live in files under one folder, so a test sets up
# GitHub's state and reads back what the plugin did to it.
#
#   claim_gh_mock_install <state_dir>
#     <state_dir>/labels        the issue's labels, one a line
#     <state_dir>/repo-label    present when the repository defines zbuild:claimed
#     <state_dir>/log           every call's arguments, one call a line
#     <state_dir>/page-<n>.json the comment pages `api --paginate` prints, in order
#                               (`api` without --paginate prints page-1.json only)
#     <state_dir>/fail-remove   present: `issue edit --remove-label` fails
#     <state_dir>/hang          present: every call blocks until <state_dir>/go
#                               appears (bounded, so no mock outlives a test)
#     <state_dir>/add-then-fail present: `issue edit --add-label` applies the label,
#                               then fails (a reply lost after GitHub acted)

claim_gh_mock_install() {
    local s="$1"
    mkdir -p "$s" "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin"
    : > "$s/labels"; : > "$s/log"
    cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh" <<MOCK
#!/usr/bin/env bash
s="$s"
printf '%s\n' "\$*" >> "\$s/log"
if [[ -e "\$s/hang" ]]; then
    for _ in \$(seq 1 300); do [[ -e "\$s/go" ]] && break; sleep 0.05; done
fi
case "\$1:\$2" in
    issue:view) cat "\$s/labels"; exit 0 ;;
    issue:edit)
        label="\${5:-}"
        if [[ "\$4" == "--add-label" ]]; then
            if [[ ! -e "\$s/repo-label" ]]; then
                printf "could not add label: '%s' not found\n" "\$label" >&2; exit 1
            fi
            /usr/bin/grep -Fxq "\$label" "\$s/labels" || printf '%s\n' "\$label" >> "\$s/labels"
            [[ -e "\$s/add-then-fail" ]] && { echo "HTTP 502: bad gateway" >&2; exit 1; }
            exit 0
        fi
        if [[ "\$4" == "--remove-label" ]]; then
            [[ -e "\$s/fail-remove" ]] && { echo "HTTP 502: bad gateway" >&2; exit 1; }
            /usr/bin/grep -Fxv "\$label" "\$s/labels" > "\$s/labels.new" || true
            mv "\$s/labels.new" "\$s/labels"; exit 0
        fi
        exit 1 ;;
    label:create) : > "\$s/repo-label"; exit 0 ;;
    api:--paginate)
        for f in "\$s"/page-*.json; do [[ -e "\$f" ]] && cat "\$f"; done; exit 0 ;;
    api:*)
        [[ -e "\$s/page-1.json" ]] && cat "\$s/page-1.json"; exit 0 ;;
esac
exit 0
MOCK
    chmod +x "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/bin/gh"
}
